reviewed_contracts.result: Existing BFloatLinearF32 only; .custom_as(...).has_value() correctly handles the optional custom schema. Its own inference requires dense rank-2 BF16 [T,K] / stored [E,K]; output must equal the inferred dense F32 [T,E]. Ordinary MatMul retains same-type input/output and F32 accumulation admission. No arbitrary mixed MatMul or rank>2 custom score contract added.

The original row-major [E,K] weight layout is re-described as column-major [K,E], preserving original BF16 pointer and leading K. The resulting logical product is [T,K] times [K,E], output [T,E]. Physical span remains E*K BF16 elements, including singleton-axis cases. No physical transpose or weight widening is added.

Geometry records data_types and element_bytes per port. Whole-element batch-stride checks, overflow/storage-span and native strided batch offsets use the correct port width. Native descriptors choose A/B BF16 and C/D F32 for scores; F32 output leading/span use4-byte elements. Ordinary matching-dtype paths therefore preserve their previous effective widths.

Compute policy still derives from input dtype: BF16 inputs use F32 accumulation, genuine F32 inputs retain PEDANTIC. Algorithms/descriptors and actual workspace are fixed during cold prepare under the existing32MiB preference cap. Shared submit/Invocation ownership, alpha/beta, caller workspace, actual queue and accepted-prefix error handling are unchanged by the before/current diff. Preparation destroys partial state and preserves the original unsupported/resource-budget fallback outcomes.

Only after the original provider returns successful admission, an actual cuBLAS candidate with two plain rank-2 inputs and one plain rank-2 output receives99, plus the unchanged Graph200 offset. No BFloatLinearF32 name, model, token count or consumer provider selection is used. Rank>2 and other families retain original rank() results; rank2 ordinary cuBLAS changes100->99 without changing the existing winner. Default policy version is2.

The previously reviewed specific fusion preferences199/200/201 remain before the new Graph leaf299. Ordinary-region eligibility uses actual discovered leaf preferences. No Graph search comparator, region matcher or fusion policy was modified in this batch. This preserves the ordering design; it does not assert globally optimal latency for all graphs.

Configured providers are already present in one Context. Array position is not a preference and all non-native base bindings use 900; the decorator supplies operation-route preferences.

Direct preparation discovers admitted candidates, filters invocation mode/alignment, sorts by proposal.preference, rejects equal-preference candidates and tries exact preparation in order. Explicit unsupported/resource-declined outcomes allow fallback; arbitrary errors do not.
